title: 🏛️ Exams 2002–2026 · relative pronouns in exam texts: who, which, that ⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2026, general) A text about "democratic learning" groups says: "The groups hold meetings where children, along with the teachers, discuss what will be taught. These are chaired by children, ___ teaches them to exchange ideas and listen to others' points of view." Tip: after a comma, a relative pronoun can stand for the whole idea before it, not only for the last noun. Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The verb "teaches" is singular, so its subject cannot be "children": the pronoun stands for the whole idea before the comma, the fact that children chair the meetings. An idea is a thing, so the pronoun is "which". "Who" is for people, "whose" would show possession, and "it" is an ordinary pronoun that cannot link the two parts of the sentence.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025, technical) A text about technical education says: "After completing an engineering or medical course, there is none ___ is jobless." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: "None" stands for a person here: no person is jobless. A person asks for "who", and "who" already is the subject of "is". "Which" is for things, "whose" would show possession, and "that he" adds a second subject after the pronoun.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024, general) A text about a volunteer says: "John discovered that the career skills ___ he has learned are put to good use." Here "he" is the subject of "has learned"; the blank stands for the skills he learned. Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: Skills are things, and a thing asks for "which". Here the pronoun is not the subject of the verb, "he" is, so "he" may follow it, unlike the sentences where who or which is the subject. "Who" is for people, "what" is not a relative pronoun after a noun, and "where" refers to a place.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021, technical) A text about green habits says: "Whenever possible, they use things ___ can be used again." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The noun before the blank is "things", so the pronoun is "which" (that would fit too). "Who" is for people and "when" is for a time. "That they" wrongly adds a second subject: the pronoun is already the subject of "can be used".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2012, technical) A father writes about his teenage daughter: "My daughter, ___ is 15, spends days and nights in front of her computer." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: "My daughter" is a person, so the pronoun is "who". "Which" is for things and "where" for places. "She" is an ordinary pronoun: it cannot link the two parts of the sentence.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2011, general) A text about transport says: "Research has shown that people ___ use public transport are healthier than ..." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: "People" are persons, so the relative pronoun is "who". "Which" is for things, "what" cannot follow a noun as a relative pronoun, and "those" is a pronoun that cannot open the group of words that describes "people".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2003) A girl describes her aunt: "She's extremely generous, but not very tolerant with people ___ don't agree with her." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The noun before the blank is "people", so the pronoun is "who". "Which" is for things and "when" for times. "That they" repeats the subject, while the pronoun already is the subject of "don't agree".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2002) Part of a sentence about tigers reads: "... meat-eating animals ___ live on land." Which word joins the two parts?
questions.explanation: The noun before the blank is "animals": a thing, an animal, so the pronoun is "which" or "that" (only "that" is offered). "Who" is for people, "what" cannot follow a noun, and "they" is an ordinary pronoun that cannot link the two parts of the sentence.
